title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 19
summary: Oil rose to the highest in almost three weeks, as a spat between the United Arab Emirates and Iran heightened regional tensions while a solution to the six-month Middle East conflict remained elusive.

title: India Says Monsoon Crop Sowing Has Recovered After July Rains
summary: India’s monsoon crop planting has largely recovered after normal July rains helped offset the driest June in 12 years, potentially easing food inflation if the precipitation persists.

title: EQT Is Said to Mull Sale of English Language Schools in Vietnam
summary: Private equity firm EQT AB is considering selling its English language education businesses in Vietnam, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

title: Copper Holds Loss as Deliveries to LME Mitigate Supply Crunch
summary: Copper declined, while readily available stocks on the London Metal Exchange swelled to ease a historic squeeze on supplies.

title: Shell Trader Mansfield Resigns After 26 Years at Oil Major
summary: Shell Plc veteran Geoffrey Mansfield has resigned from his role as global desk lead for low-carbon fuels trading, according to a person familiar with the matter.

title: Three Chinese Tankers U-Turn in Hormuz as Risks Remain High
summary: Three China-linked supertankers have U-turned in the Strait of Hormuz as risks to shipping remain elevated, with prospects for a normalization of traffic dimming after President Donald Trump took a hard line on Iran.

title: Copper's Upward Trend Can Continue, BlackRock Says
summary: "The trend is very much your friend," says Evy Hambro, head of fundamental equities thematic and sector investing at BlackRock, when asked about the rise in copper prices. "We are seeing a very tight market," he tells Bloomberg Television. "It's very easy to say: well, okay, it's gone up a lot and we should ignore it, and it's too late. The reality is, if you've done that you've missed out." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Libyan Protests Flare as Government Struggles to Keep Lights On
summary: Protests broke out again in the Libyan capital after the energy-rich country suffered its third widespread blackout in two days, fueling public anger over deteriorating basic services.

title: Bond Traders Are Hedging the Risk Fed Pivots to Cuts in 2027
summary: Bond traders are changing gears again. After a raft of data helped all but price out interest-rate hikes for the rest of the year, wagers in the options market are looking to hedge the risk that the Federal Reserve pivots to cutting rates in 2027.

title: Stocks and Bonds Find Respite After Days of Strain: Markets Wrap
summary: Stocks halted losses and bonds caught some respite as a measure of calm returned to markets after days that saw yields at levels not seen in decades.

title: Egypt Bond Risk at 2014 Low Shows Decade of Debt Distress Easing
summary: Record foreign-currency reserves and a vote of confidence from the International Monetary Fund have cut Egypt’s risk premium to the lowest since 2014.

title: Pakistan’s Record IPO Year Gets Boost From SE Fruits Listing
summary: Fresh produce company SE Fruits and Vegetable Ltd. is planning an initial public offering in Pakistan next month to boost its export capacity, adding to a record year of listings in the country.

title: Absa CEO: Africa Expansion Plan Progressing Well
summary: Absa Group is exploring the possibility of converting its representative office in Nigeria into a merchant bank. Chief Executive Officer Kenny Fihla also said he sees opportunities in Uganda, Zambia, Tanzania, Angola. He spoke to Bloomberg’s Chief Africa correspondent, Jennifer Zabasajja, to discuss their plans after the group reported net income for the first half-year of 12.58 billion rand vs. 11.23 billion rand y/y. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Evergrande Liquidators Challenge Hong Kong Watchdog in Court
summary: A Hong Kong court began hearing arguments on whether a deal that set up a fund to compensate China Evergrande minority shareholders is valid.

title: PHP/USD: Record-Low Philippine Peso Invites Central Bank Intervention
summary: The Philippine peso fell to a record low against the dollar as oil prices climbed, putting more pressure on the central bank to take action.

title: CXMT Rival YMTC Moves Closer to China’s Next Big Chip IPO
summary: Yangtze Memory Technologies Co. moved closer to an initial public offering in China, following in the footsteps of rival CXMT Corp.’s near-record share sale.

title: Japan’s Topix Falls Most Since March as Tech Selloff Accelerates
summary: Japan’s stocks slumped, with the Topix benchmark dropping the most since March, as anxiety over surging bond yields sapped risk appetite and weighed on AI-related stocks.

title: Stockland Rises Most Since 1987 as Tax Rules Favor New Builds
summary: Shares of two of Australia’s largest property developers surged, with Stockland seeing its largest advance in about 40 years, as tax changes favoring new builds offered a potential boost to residential development.

title: UK Inflation Accelerates as Energy Bills Surge
summary: UK consumer prices climbed to a four-month high after energy bills rose, ending a short period of respite for hard-pressed British households. Matt Bunny of Bloomberg Economics has the details. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Adnoc Cuts to Murban Volumes Send Flagship Oil Grade Higher
summary: Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. plans to trim the amount of crude sold to Asian customers in August and September, according to people familiar with the matter — cuts that are already helping to push up the price of the flagship Murban oil grade.
